name: Time clauses: when, while, before, after, until
subtitle: A time clause says when something happens: when, while, before, after, as soon as, until. For the future, use the present simple after these words: I'll call you when I get home.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-b1 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: When I get home, I'll call you. · I'll wait until you come back.

qa.html: A time clause says when something happens. It starts with a time word (when, while, before, after, as soon as, until) and has its own subject and verb. I'll call you when I get home.

For the future, use the present simple after the time word. Don't use will there. As soon as I get home, I'll call you. The main clause can have will. You can use the present perfect if you want to say "finished": I'll call you when I've finished.
Time clause first? Put a comma after it. When I arrive, I'll text you. Main clause first? No comma. I'll text you when I arrive.

When = at that time. While = at the same time (a longer action): I read while I wait. Before and after show the order. As soon as = immediately. Until = up to that moment (till is informal): Wait here until I come back.

Typical mistakes: ✗ When I will arrive, I'll call you. → ✓ When I arrive, I'll call you. · ✗ I'll wait until you will come. → ✓ …until you come. · ✗ I'll wait while you come back. → ✓ …until you come back. (while = at the same time, until = up to a moment)

concept.noteHtml: For past events, use past tenses in the time clause: When I got home, I called her. The words before and after can also come before a noun: before lunch, after work. See Time prepositions. For the difference between when and if, see When or if. For will and other future forms, see Future forms.

No comma when the time clause comes second.

listen.text: When I get home, I'll call you.
listen.note: The meaning is future, but the time clause uses the present simple: get, not will get. A comma follows the time clause.

listen.text: I'll wait here until you come back.
listen.note: Until means up to that moment. After until, use the present simple.

listen.text: She listens to music while she cooks.
listen.note: While means at the same time. Two actions happen together.

rounds.label: 1 · The future: present simple after the time word
rounds.instruction: You hear two sentences and a time word. Join them. Use the present simple after the time word.

example.prompt: I'll call you. I get home. – when
example.answer: I'll call you when I get home.

items.prompt: I'll text you. I arrive. – as soon as
items.answer: I'll text you as soon as I arrive.

items.prompt: We'll wait. The bus comes. – until
items.answer: We'll wait until the bus comes.

items.prompt: I'll cook dinner. You get home. – before
items.answer: I'll cook dinner before you get home.

items.prompt: We'll have a coffee. The film ends. – after
items.answer: We'll have a coffee after the film ends.

items.prompt: She'll phone you. She finishes work. – when
items.answer: She'll phone you when she finishes work.

items.prompt: Tom will help us. He has time. – as soon as
items.answer: Tom will help us as soon as he has time.

rounds.label: 2 · Time clause first
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence. Say it again and start with the time word.

example.prompt: I'll call you when I get home.
example.answer: When I get home, I'll call you.

items.prompt: I'll text you as soon as I arrive.
items.answer: As soon as I arrive, I'll text you.

items.prompt: I'll lock the door before I leave.
items.answer: Before I leave, I'll lock the door.

items.prompt: We'll have lunch after the meeting ends.
items.answer: After the meeting ends, we'll have lunch.

items.prompt: I'll phone you when I finish work.
items.answer: When I finish work, I'll phone you.

items.prompt: She'll set the table while he cooks.
items.answer: While he cooks, she'll set the table.

items.prompt: Tom will help us as soon as he has time.
items.answer: As soon as he has time, Tom will help us.

exercises.title: Choose the time word.
exercises.hint: Think about the order of the two events and whether they happen together.
exercises.hintHtml: before / afterWhich event comes first?whileTwo things happen at the same time.untilSomething continues up to a moment.as soon asImmediately when something happens.

items.prompt: Wait here ___ I come back.
items.why: You wait up to the moment I come back: until.

items.prompt: I'll text you ___ I arrive.
items.why: The text comes immediately when I arrive: as soon as.

items.prompt: Priya reads a book ___ she waits for the bus.
items.why: Reading and waiting happen at the same time: while.

items.prompt: Brush your teeth ___ you go to bed.
items.why: You brush your teeth first, then you go to bed: before.

items.prompt: We'll have a coffee ___ the film finishes.
items.why: First the film finishes, then the coffee: after.

items.prompt: I'll stay at work ___ I finish this report.
items.why: I stay up to the moment the report is finished: until.

items.prompt: Don't talk ___ the teacher is explaining.
items.why: Her explaining and your talking happen together: while.

items.prompt: Please read the rules ___ you start the test.
items.why: You read first, then you start: before.

exercises.title: Choose the right verb form.
exercises.hint: After a time word, use the present simple for the future. Use the past simple for the past.
exercises.hintHtml: present simpleIn the time clause, for the future or a habit.willOnly in the main clause, not after the time word.

items.prompt: When I ___ home, I'll call you.
items.why: Future meaning: present simple after when, not will get.

items.prompt: I'll wait until you ___ ready.
items.why: Future meaning: present simple after until.

items.prompt: As soon as the film ___, we'll go home.
items.why: Future meaning: present simple after as soon as.

items.prompt: I was cooking when the phone ___.
items.why: This is a story in the past, so use the past simple.

items.prompt: While I ___ for the bus, I usually read the news.
items.why: A habit: present simple. With I, use wait.

items.prompt: We'll have lunch after Mum ___ here.
items.why: Future meaning: present simple. With Mum (she), use arrives.

items.prompt: I'll let you know before I ___ tomorrow.
items.why: Future meaning: present simple after before.

items.prompt: Yesterday I called her as soon as I ___ home.
items.why: Yesterday is in the past: got.

pairs.a: First I call, then I leave.

pairs.q: I'll call you after I leave.

pairs.q: I'll call you as soon as I leave.
pairs.a: I call you the moment I leave.

pairs.a: The time clause comes first, so there is a comma.
